Home » News » Business » The Halal Shack to replace Subway in Michigan Union
Posted inBusiness

The Halal Shack to replace Subway in Michigan Union

by Kevin Gonzaga September 27, 2026September 27, 2026

Share this:

  • Share on X (Opens in new window) X
  • Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:12
Instaread

Students returning to campus in fall 2026 may have noticed a change in food options at the University of Michigan Union basement. Subway’s former storefront, located next to Panda Express and Wing Snob, was permanently closed.

Following renovations to the Union from 2018 to 2020, only two restaurant vendors returned: Subway — formerly one of nine franchise locations in Ann Arbor — and Panda Express. They joined a new lineup that included Blue Market and Panera Bread. According to University officials, Subway’s lease ended at the end of April, shortly after the winter semester wrapped up. 

However, a new restaurant will take Subway’s place in winter 2027: The Halal Shack. The New York-based Mediterranean restaurant chain will be the first business to open in the Union since Wing Snob first welcomed customers in August 2024.

In an email to The Daily, Susan Pile, senior director of University Unions and Auxiliary Services, wrote The Halal Shack was chosen — with the help of students —  because of its philosophy. 

Discover more
Food
Fast Food
food

“Students serving on our advisory boards played an important role in selecting (Subway’s) replacement, The Halal Shack, as part of a Request for Proposal process,” Pile wrote. “We’re excited to welcome The Halal Shack to the Michigan Union, with an expected opening in the winter 2027 semester. Its mission to unite people through food closely aligns with University Unions’ role in cultivating community and belonging at the University of Michigan.”

Several other chains that have closed in Ann Arbor recently, including both Buffalo Wild Wings and Bruegger’s Bagels in May, highlighting the difficulty of maintaining businesses amid rising expenses associated with rent and post-pandemic changes.

In an interview with The Michigan Daily, LSA sophomore Omar Rashid said although he was surprised this particular location closed, he understands the decision considering the reported financial troubles several Subway franchise owners have faced in recent years.

Discover more
Weddings
Restaurants
Geographic Reference

“I was a little bit surprised, but I have heard in the news that Subway in general is having some financial issues,” Rashid said. “I think they are closing down a lot of locations if they’re not getting enough business. I imagine this place as well is very expensive to rent out, so that might’ve played a role.”

In an interview with The Daily, LSA sophomore Jonatan Contreras, who worked at Michigan Dining over the summer, said the drop in spending activity in the summer can cause businesses to struggle.

“Compared to the school year, when we have lunch rushes lasting hours, the summer is essentially quiet all day long,” Contreras said. “Not like a complete ghost town, but definitely diminished foot traffic. I feel like that is definitely a key part of which businesses survive in Ann Arbor and which don’t.”

In an interview with The Daily, LSA freshman Diego Peralta said The Halal Shack will provide students with a new, more diverse option for on campus dining.

“I would say Subway is pretty boring — you can find Subways anywhere,” Peralta said. “But, you don’t see halal food very often, so for me, that’s a far better option that I would much rather prefer on campus.”

Daily Staff Reporter Kevin Gonzaga can be reached at kgonzaga@umich.edu.
